newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty firmer vs basket, one-day revrepo rate up.
newsitem.headline: Zloty firmer vs basket, one-day revrepo rate up.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed against the basket of currencies on a light currency-selling trend on inflows from exchange bureaux which prevented the unit from falling despite a stronger world dollar, dealers said.
They said the currency selling was likley to be seasonal because of increased cross border shopping in Poland before the Christmas holidays.

"A simple explanation of the slight currency ovresupply on the market is that it comes from a seasonal inflow from exchange bureaux before the (Christmas) holidays," said one dealer at a foreign bank here.

The zloty closed up at 2.96/2.93 percent from the parity rate against Friday's close at 2.91/2.83 percent. It closed at 2.8615/27 to the dollar, down from 2.8505/25 on Friday and at 1.8403/09 to the mark, up from 1.8520/30.
Poland had a current account deficit of $425 million in October bringing the shortfall in the January-October period to $859 million, the National Bank of Poland said.

The NBP has earlier said the deteriorating current account with the deficit expected at about $3.9 billion next year from this year's expected $300 million would strongly limit the zloty's upside potential.
Analysts said that so far the zloty was well protected from falling by a constant flow of currencies from privatisation deals and capital increases of foreign companies operating in Poland.

"Unless the central bank would take the cost of intervention, the zloty is likely to occupy a strong position at three percent from parity with some 0.2 point swings," said Marcin Stefaniuk from Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA.
One-day deposit rates eased under the pressure of reserve surpluses of some banks, but rates were undrepinned at 21 percent by the central bank's reverse repo rate.
The NBP drained 689 million zlotys off the market for one-day raising the maximum accepted rate by 0.2 point to 21.50 percent.
Dealers said the market was fairly liquid on Monday, but rates were unlikely to fall below the level signalled by the central bank.
Overnight rates were at 21.00/22.00 percent from opening's 22.0/22.4 percent, tomorrow/next rates were at 21.00/22.00 percent, down from 22.0/22.45 percent.
